operations.title: Install DROP namespace guard
operations.notes: Database superuser only. Installs a fixed SECURITY DEFINER SQL function in pg_catalog to retain the native namespace and relation catalog-row locks for reviewed table DROP by table/schema owners. The function checks the invoking session or SET ROLE ownership and grants no catalog update privileges. Installation is CREATE only: an existing function is never overwritten. Inspect an existing collision before retrying. Required per database for ordinary owners, including older PostgreSQL minors whose schema rename ignores object locks. No automatic installation, SQL replay or restart. The reviewed installer explicitly grants PUBLIC EXECUTE; the fixed body restricts use to native table/schema owners. It does not grant catalog or table privileges.

operations.notes: Native extended-statistics lifecycle. Column/expression operands and multivariate kinds are distinct typed grids. Single expression has no multivariate kinds. Captured OID/table/kinds/definition remain native. DDN create supports exact source dependency and rediscovered identities. Uses the retained administration review, permissions, transaction/cleanup and no automatic replay.

operations.title: Grant parameter privileges

fields.label: Parameter
fields.help: Use a catalog parameter name, never a setting value.

operations.notes: Native PostgreSQL15+ pg_parameter_acl. Target native parname/OID and typed SET/ALTER SYSTEM privileges, roles, grant option and explicit CASCADE/RESTRICT. No configuration values enter requests, plans or inventory. Native grant authority is independent of application administer/execute permission. Inspection reports explicit ACL rows and native current-principal privileges, without inferring that a missing row allows access. Shared cluster ACLs are inspected via the server inventory; runtime gate is checked at review and apply. Native grants do not SET or ALTER SYSTEM a value. Transactional native acknowledgement and cleanup; no automatic replay.

operations.title: Grant default privileges
operations.notes: Selected-database native ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES. Explicit current or named creation owners, FOR ROLE/USER, global or selected-schema scope; all native families including SCHEMAS and LARGE OBJECTS (18+). MAINTAIN requires17+. SCHEMAS/LARGE OBJECTS reject IN SCHEMA. Grant-option-only revocation and CASCADE/RESTRICT retain native semantics. Future objects only: existing ACLs are not changed, and role membership does not merge other owners default privileges. Inspect/readback returns native default-ACL OIDs and explicit grant entries; an absent row means native built-in defaults, never inferred denial. Selectors are explicit, not inferred from a selected catalog row. Shared retained review/apply permissions, transaction, cleanup and no replay; no values or secrets.

operations.title: Checkpoint

fields.label: Wait timeout (milliseconds)
fields.help: 1–600000. Stops waiting; checkpoint work may continue.

operations.notes: Standalone native CHECKPOINT on an independent autocommit attachment, bound at review/apply to the actual server/startup/database and effective/authenticated principals. Native superuser or native checkpoint-role authority is required, independently of application administer/execute permissions. Exact CHECKPOINT command tag is required. Receipt separates nontransactional completion and connection release; rollback never undoes a checkpoint. Timeout, cancellation and lost acknowledgement have unknown effect; no automatic replay and no physical durability inference. Synchronous bounded wait; no progress stream or manual cancellation API is advertised.
